decisive_items: violaceous pretibial lesions with areas of necrosis
pretibial lesions of violaceous coloration, similar to retiform purpura
response.rationale: CKD with diabetes and painful retiform purpura progressing to necrosis strongly suggests calciphylaxis. HIT is less likely because platelet count is normal and lesions are not at heparin injection sites; APS is contradicted by negative autoimmunity studies; warfarin-induced necrosis lacks warfarin exposure.

rejected.why: Negative autoimmunity studies and no clear thrombotic event beyond atrial fibrillation, making antiphospholipid syndrome unlikely.
No warfarin exposure is mentioned; the patient received heparin, not warfarin.
Platelet count is normal (173×10⁹/L) and skin lesions are not at the heparin injection site, making heparin-induced thrombocytopenia less likely.
